claim: Economics and engineering fields have made effective use of parametric models for complex multivariate time series.
source: Whereas other fields that grapple with complex multivariate time series have made effective use of parametric models such as economics and engineering (Kim et al., 1998; Blanchard and Simon, 2001; West, 1996), neuroscientists largely ceded early parametric approaches (e.g. linear autoregressive models) in favor of non-parametric spectral decomposition methods, as a means of uncovering features of neural activity that may correlate with behavior.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work in economics and engineering.

claim: This paper presents the first major application of stochastic volatility models to neural time-series data.
source: This paper presents the first major application of stochastic volatility models to neural time-series data.
evidence: This is stated as a contribution of the paper.

claim: The use of a multivariate modeling approach allows accounting for interactions between different subregions in the MTL and thus provides a better fit to the neural data than a univariate approach.
source: The use of a multivariate modeling approach allows us to account for interactions between different subregions in the MTL and thus provides a better fit to the neural data than a univariate approach.
evidence: This is a summary of the model comparison findings.

claim: The MSV model fully captures how changes in neural data measured by volatility in one region influences changes in another region.
source: Our MSV model fully captures how changes in neural data measured by volatility in one region influences changes in another region, providing insights into the complex dynamics of neural brain signals.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the MSV model.

claim: Volatility can be a promising biomarker due to its broadband nature.
source: We further demonstrated that volatility can be a promising biomarker due to its broadband nature by comparing its performance to one of spectral power in classifying subsequent memory.
evidence: This is an inference from the classification findings.

claim: Researchers can extend these models to broader classes of neural recordings.
source: Finally, researchers can extend these models to broader classes of neural recordings, and exploit their statistical power to substantially increase our understanding of how behavior emerges from the complex interplay of neural activity across many brain regions.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future applications.

claim: 96 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy undergoing intracranial electroencephalographic monitoring were recruited in this study.
source: Ninety six patients with drug-resistant epilepsy undergoing intracranial electroencephalographic monitoring were recruited in this study.
evidence: This describes the participant population.

claim: Data were collected as part of a study of the effects of electrical stimulation on memory-related brain function at multiple medical centers.
source: Data were collected as part of a study of the effects of electrical stimulation on memory-related brain function at multiple medical centers.
evidence: This describes the data collection context.

claim: The research protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board at each hospital and informed consent was obtained from each participant.
source: The research protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board at each hospital and informed consent was obtained from each participant.
evidence: This describes the ethical approval and consent process.

claim: Electrophysiological signals were collected from electrodes implanted subdurally on the cortical surface and within brain parenchyma.
source: Electrophysiological signals were collected from electrodes implanted subdurally on the cortical surface and within brain parenchyma.
evidence: This describes the data collection method.

claim: The neurosurgeons at each clinical site determined the placement of electrodes to best localize epileptogenic regions.
source: The neurosurgeons at each clinical site determined the placement of electrodes to best localize epileptogenic regions.
evidence: This describes the electrode placement procedure.

claim: Each word presentation lasts for 1600 ms followed by a blank inter-stimulus interval (ISI) of 800 to 1200 ms.
source: Each word presentation lasts for 1600 ms followed by a blank inter-stimulus interval (ISI) of 800 to 1200 ms.
evidence: This describes the experimental timing.

claim: Subjects were asked to perform a math distraction task immediately after the presentation of the last word to mitigate the recency effect and the primacy effect.
source: To mitigate the recency effect (recalling last items best) and the primacy effect (recalling first items better than the middle items), subjects were asked to perform a math distraction task immediately after the presentation of the last word.
evidence: This describes the experimental design rationale.

claim: The delay math task lasted for 20 s.
source: The delay math task lasted for 20 s, after which subjects were asked to recall as many words as possible from the recent list of words, in any order during the 30 s recall period.
evidence: This describes the experimental timing.

claim: Subjects performed up to 25 lists per session of recording (300 words).
source: Subjects performed up to 25 lists per session of recording (300 words).
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: iEEG signals were recorded from subdural and depth electrodes at various sampling rates (500, 1000, or 1600 Hz).
source: iEEG signals were recorded from subdural and depth electrodes at various sampling rates (500, 1000, or 1600 Hz) based on the the amplifier and the preference of the clinical team using one of the following EEG systems: DeltaMed XlTek (Natus), Grass Telefactor, and Nihon-Kohden.
evidence: This describes the data acquisition parameters.

claim: A 5 Hz band-stop fourth order Butterworth filter centered on 60 Hz was applied to attenuate signal from electrical noise.
source: We applied a 5 Hz band-stop fourth order Butterworth filter centered on 60 Hz to attenuate signal from electrical noise.
evidence: This describes the data preprocessing.

claim: The data were re-referenced using the common average of all electrodes in the MTL to eliminate potentially confounding large-scale artifacts and noise.
source: We re-referenced the data using the common average of all electrodes in the MTL to eliminate potentially confounding large-scale artifacts and noise.
evidence: This describes the data preprocessing.

claim: Morlet wavelet transform (wave number = 5) was used to compute power as a function of time for iEEG signals.
source: We used Morlet wavelet transform (wave number = 5) to compute power as a function of time for our iEEG signals.
evidence: This describes the spectral analysis method.

claim: The frequencies were sampled linearly from 3 to 180 Hz with 1 Hz increments.
source: The frequencies were sample linearly from 3 to 180 Hz with 1 Hz increments.
evidence: This describes the spectral analysis parameters.

claim: For each electrode and frequency, spectral power was log-transformed and then averaged over the encoding period.
source: For each electrode and frequency, spectral power was log-transformed and then averaged over the encoding period.
evidence: This describes the feature extraction procedure.

claim: Within a session of recording, the spectral power was z-scored using the distribution of power features across events.
source: Within a session of recording, the spectral power was z-scored using the distribution of power features across events.
evidence: This describes the normalization procedure.

claim: The MSV model was applied to the dataset constructed from the encoding events with an assumption that the parameters governing the dynamics of the volatility process does not change within a session of recording.
source: To extract volatility feature, we applied the MSV model to the dataset constructed from the encoding events with an assumption that the parameters governing the dynamics of the volatility process does not change within a session of recording, that is the parameters of the MSV model are assumed to be shared across encoding events.
evidence: This describes the modeling assumption.

claim: The common average reference was used to remove large-scale noise from MTL recordings.
source: In the present manuscript, we used the common average reference (of MTL electrodes) to remove large-scale noise from our MTL recordings.
evidence: This describes the referencing choice.

claim: Connectivity between a pair of adjacent bipolar electrodes is contaminated by signal common to their shared monopolar contact.
source: First, connectivity between a pair of adjacent bipolar electrodes is contaminated by signal common to their shared monopolar contact; as such, it is difficult to interpret connectivity between such pairs.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of bipolar referencing.

claim: Bipolar re-referencing within the MTL produces the undesirable outcome that a bipolar midpoint 'virtual' electrode could fall in a subregion where neither physical contact was placed.
source: Second, bipolar re-referencing within the MTL produces the undesirable outcome that a bipolar midpoint 'virtual' electrode could fall in a subregion where neither physical contact was placed, making observed connectivities difficult to interpret.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of bipolar referencing.

claim: Hippocampal subfields and MTL cortices were automatically labeled in a pre-implant 2 mm thick T2-weighted MRI using the Automatic segmentation of hippocampal subfields (ASHS) multi-atlas segmentation method.
source: Hippocampal subfields and MTL cortices were automatically labeled in a pre-implant 2 mm thick T2-weighted MRI using the Automatic segmentation of hippocampal subfields (ASHS) multi-atlas segmentation method (Yushkevich et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the anatomical localization method with citation.

claim: A post-implant CT was co-registered with the MRI using Advanced Normalization Tools.
source: A post-implant was co-registered with the MRI using Advanced Normalization Tools (Avants et al., 2008).
evidence: This describes the image registration method with citation.

claim: MTL depth electrodes that were visible in the CT were localized by a pair of neuroradiologists with expertise in MTL anatomy.
source: MTL depth electrodes that were visible in the CT were then localized by a pair of neuroradiologists with expertise in MTL anatomy.
evidence: This describes the electrode localization procedure.

claim: Classical statistical tests were applied on the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate of the parameter of interest to assess an effect across subjects.
source: To assess an effect across subjects, we applied classical statistical tests on the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate of the parameter of interest .
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis approach.

claim: This approach has been used in many Bayesian applications to FMRI studies to test an effect across subjects.
source: This approach has been used in many Bayesian applications to FMRI studies (Stephan et al., 2010) to test an effect across subjects.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Gaussian regression models were applied to take the correlations among frequencies into account for analyses concerning frequencies.
source: For analyses concerning frequencies, we applied Gaussian regression models (Rasmussen, 2004) to take the correlations among frequencies into account.
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis method with citation.

claim: The Matern (5/2) kernel function was used for all analyses that used Gaussian regression models, which enforces that the underlying functional form be at least twice differentiable.
source: We used the Matern (5/2) kernel function for all analyses that used Gaussian regression models, which enforces that the underlying functional form be at least twice differentiable.
evidence: This describes the kernel choice for Gaussian regression.
